subject: Access egress whitelist + service identity runbook sync
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@finrise.com>, Elena Torres <elena.torres@finrise.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Access egress whitelist + service identity runbook sync

Hi Sanjay / Elena,

Thanks again for the kickoff yesterday. To keep the implementation moving this week I wanted to align on two parallel tracks we typically run for enterprise customers: 1) network egress / IP allowlist prep and 2) service identity & SCIM/service account mapping.

High-level plan (proposed):
- Egress/IP allowlist: you provide CIDR ranges and testing IPs -> we validate from our infra -> coordinate a 30-min cutover window.
- Service identities: shared inventory of service accounts that will call Redwood APIs (machine users), plus a SCIM mapping for Okta/Azure AD.
- SSO (SAML): we have your IDP metadata and will produce an SP metadata file to drop into your config.

Immediate ask: please confirm the person owning firewall changes and provide an initial list of public egress IPs (or NAT ranges) you expect us to allow by EOD Wednesday. I attached a lightweight template to capture CIDRs and a service-account inventory we can use.

Attachments referenced below — you can reply inline or upload to the shared MAP link: https://redwood.app/drive/FR-3872-MAP

Attached (stubs):
- egress_whitelist_template.csv (CSV, 2KB)
- service-account-inventory.xlsx (XLSX, 12KB)

Proposed times for a 30-min cutover test: July 4 or July 5 between 10:00-14:00 PT. Suggest we aim for July 5 so internal teams have a day to review your ranges.

I'll loop in Soojin for the SCIM readiness check and Monica for service-account provisioning.

Thanks,
Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

On Mon, Jul 1, 2028 at 9:12 AM Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Sanjay / Elena,
> 
> Thanks again for the kickoff yesterday. To keep the implementation moving this week I wanted to align on two parallel tracks we typically run for enterprise customers: 1) network egress / IP allowlist prep and 2) service identity & SCIM/service account mapping.

Thanks Marcus — this looks good. A few clarifications from our side so we can populate your templates: 

1) Environment: FinRise infra sits behind an Azure NAT gateway and we have a small static egress pool of three public IPs for outbound traffic. We also have a separate set of IPs for our staging environment.
2) Cutover constraints: our security team requires a 48-hour change advisory for production firewall changes; staging can be more flexible.
3) Service accounts: we use Azure AD for SCIM. We’ll need the SCIM schema mapping for identity.email -> userPrincipalName and a column for 'role' so our provisioning scripts can create Azure groups.

Can you confirm whether Redwood requires inbound firewall rules to Redwood-managed nodes, or if outbound allowlisting from our edge to Redwood is sufficient? Also, provide the SP metadata you mentioned so we can have our IdP team pre-configure.

We’ll populate the CSV and the inventory by EOD Wednesday but need the SP metadata and a list of your test IPs today if possible.

Thanks,
Sanjay Patel
Head of IT Operations
FinRise
sanjay@finrise.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@finrise.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Elena Torres <elena.torres@finrise.com>
Date: 2028-07-03T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Access egress whitelist + service identity runbook sync

Thanks Sanjay — good questions. Quick answers and the operational plan: 

- Network: outbound allowlisting from FinRise to Redwood is sufficient for the standard API flow. You do not need to open inbound ports on your side. We will, however, ask for static source IPs (your NAT) so we can allow those on our egress/ingress proxies for whitelisting and rate-limiting exemptions. For staging you can provide the staging NAT pool.

- SP metadata: attached (saml_metadata.xml) and also uploaded to the MAP link. Use the ACS URL and EntityID from the file; if your IdP team needs certificate fingerprint only we can provide that too.

- SCIM mapping: Soojin will share our recommended SCIM mapping for Azure AD. In brief: userName -> userPrincipalName, active -> accountEnabled, emails[type=work].value -> mail, plus custom attribute for department/role. We'll also include a small example CSV for bulk provisioning.

Operational timeline (proposed):
1) By EOD Wed (Jul 3): FinRise provides production NAT CIDRs + staging NAT CIDRs (you confirmed EOD Wed for CSV).
2) Thu (Jul 4): Redwood validates CIDRs from our side and shares preflight report (no changes required).
3) Fri (Jul 5): 30-min production cutover window (target 10:30–11:00 PT). Redwood will run a connectivity smoke test and verify token issuance for a sample service account.

Attachments included (stubs):
- saml_metadata.xml (XML, 6KB)
- egress_whitelist_template.csv (CSV, 2KB)
- service-account-inventory.xlsx (XLSX, 12KB)

Next steps for your team: upload the filled CSV and the inventory to the MAP link or reply with them attached. For the 48-hour CAB constraint we can treat Friday as a staging dry-run and schedule production the following Monday if needed — please confirm which you'd prefer.

Soojin, Monica — can you confirm SCIM attributes and the sample service-account that we should use for the smoke test?

Thanks,
Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

--

Thanks all — quick operational notes from CS/Provisioning: 
- For the smoke test please use the service-account ID: redwood-smoke@finrise (we'll pre-create it in SCIM and set role=integration).
- Rotation cadence: recommend a 90-day key rotation for service accounts that have long-lived tokens; if FinRise prefers shorter we can enforce a 30-day TTL via token policy.
- Post-cutover validation: we'll request a simple API call from your staging NAT and one from prod NAT to confirm headers and rate-limiting behavior.

Sanjay/Elena — given your CAB window, what is your preference: a Fri staging dry-run + Mon prod, or Fri prod directly (we can accommodate but will need explicit CAB approval)?

Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
